title: Six top-level tabs; two hidden in More
evidence: TabView (lines 5-12) declares six tabs: Today, Trends, Workouts, Awards, Sharing, Settings. On iPhone a TabView with more than five items shows four tabs plus a system More tab, so Sharing and Settings move into a nested More list and the tab bar stops showing what the app contains. Count: 6 against the platform limit of 5. Fix: consolidate to five areas (Settings as a toolbar button or profile sheet, Awards inside Trends or Today) and use value-based tabs: TabView(selection: $tab) { Tab("Today", systemImage: "calendar", value: .today) { TodayView() } ... }.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable), which stays a tab bar on iPhone and becomes a sidebar on iPad.

title: Trends tab root has no navigation title
evidence: TrendsView (lines 16-22) wraps its List in a NavigationStack with no .navigationTitle, while the other five tab roots set one. The screen never says where the user is, and anything later pushed from it gets a back button that reads "Back". Fix: List { Text("This week") }.navigationTitle("Trends"), matching the tab label.

title: Self-view drag offset held in @State strands on cancel
evidence: CallScreen keeps the live drag translation in @State dragOffset (line 43), writes it in .onChanged (line 54) and clears it only inside .onEnded (line 59). .onEnded does not run when the system cancels the gesture (incoming call, Control Center, a parent claiming the touch), so the camera tile is left stranded off its corner and the next drag starts with a jump. Inferred from source; system cancellation needs a device run. Fix: @GestureState(reset: { _, t in t.animation = UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.2) }) private var drag: CGSize = .zero; .offset(drag); DragGesture(coordinateSpace: .named("stage")).updating($drag) { v, s, _ in s = v.translation }.onEnded { v in withAnimation(settle) { corner = .nearest(to: reduceMotion ? v.location : v.predictedEndLocation, in: stageSize) } }, and delete dragOffset.

title: What's New sheet disables swipe-dismiss with nothing to lose
evidence: WhatsNewSheet ends with .interactiveDismissDisabled() (no argument, so true) on a read-only list of release notes. There is no input to protect, so the reflexive swipe-down does nothing and Done is the only exit; the sheet feels stuck. This is not the required-step exception (a consent sheet with Accept and Decline). Fix: delete line 148 and keep the Done button.

title: List-plus-detail ships as one column at regular width
evidence: ContentView is a list that pushes WorkoutDetail inside a single NavigationStack (lines 10-23). At regular width (iPad, or the iPad build on a Mac) the list fills the window and the detail then replaces it: one column, no sidebar, the stretched-phone layout. Measurement: on a 1024pt landscape iPad window the detail VStack is .frame(maxWidth: .infinity) plus .padding() (16pt per side), so its text measure is 1024 - 32 = 992pt (97% of the window) with no reading cap, and each list row puts the name and the calorie value at opposite ends of the same full-width row. Assumes an iPad target; the snippet does not declare its device family. Fix: NavigationSplitView { List(workouts, selection: $selection) { WorkoutRow(workout: $0) }.navigationTitle("Workouts") } detail: { if let w = workouts.first(where: { $0.id == selection }) { WorkoutDetail(workout: w) } else { ContentUnavailableView("Select a Workout", systemImage: "figure.run") } }, and cap the detail with .frame(maxWidth: 700, alignment: .leading).frame(maxWidth: .infinity).

title: Pushed detail shows its name twice as large titles
evidence: WorkoutDetail sets .navigationTitle(workout.name) with the default .automatic display mode, which inherits the large title from the Workouts root, and its content opens with Text(workout.name).font(.largeTitle) (line 32). Inferred from source: the screen stacks the same name twice in large type, and a large title on a pushed screen reads as another root. Fix: .navigationTitle(workout.name).navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline), keeping the in-content heading (or keep the large title and drop the Text, not both).

title: Volume dial wraps between 0% and 100% at top
evidence: VolumeDial assigns the raw angle on every sample: volume = fraction(at: value.location) (line 216), and fraction() maps atan2 onto 0..<2pi (lines 227-231). Just right of the top the value is ~0%, just left of it ~100%, so a finger crossing 12 o'clock moves the alert volume from silent to full (or back) in a one-point move, and a touch-down anywhere on the ring teleports the value. The rest of the control is well built (ScaledMetric size, Slider accessibilityRepresentation). Fix: accumulate the unwrapped delta and clamp instead of assigning the angle: @GestureState private var previousAngle: Double? = nil; DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).updating($previousAngle) { value, previous, _ in let a = angle(at: value.location); if let p = previous { var d = a - p; if d > .pi { d -= 2 * .pi } else if d < -.pi { d += 2 * .pi }; volume = min(max(volume + d / (2 * .pi), 0), 1) }; previous = a }, where angle(at:) returns the atan2 value fraction(at:) computes today.

title: Volume dial outgrows the window at AX5
evidence: @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body) var diameter = 120 (line 200) drives .frame(width: diameter, height: diameter) (line 212). Body text is 17pt at Large and 53pt at AX5, so the dial becomes 120 x 53/17 = 374pt square inside a Form row. Measurement: 374pt against a 320pt narrowest window is 54pt too wide before the Form's own row margins, so the ring overflows its row on every iPhone width at AX5; inferred from source, the minimumDistance: 0 drag on a 374pt-tall target also takes most vertical scroll attempts that start on it. Configuration: AX5, 320-375pt window. Fix: keep the scaling but bound it: @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body) private var scaledDiameter: CGFloat = 120; private var diameter: CGFloat { min(scaledDiameter, 220) } (fraction(at:) keeps using diameter).

title: ViewThatFits fallback is the same HStack, so nothing fits
evidence: Both ViewThatFits candidates (lines 11-16 and 17-22) are one-line HStacks of icon, label, Spacer and value; the second only drops spacing from 16 to 8. When the first overflows, the system renders the last candidate anyway, so at large sizes the row compresses and the label or value wraps or truncates, which is exactly what ViewThatFits was added to prevent. Measurement: candidate 2 recovers 3 gaps x 8pt = 24pt; AX5 scales both Text views by 53/17 = 3.1x, so a label and value measuring 150pt at Large need ~468pt at AX5 against a 320pt window less 64pt fixed (32pt icon frame + 2 x 16pt padding). The 32 x 32 icon frames (lines 12 and 18) stay 32pt while the symbol grows with body text. Configuration: AX5, 320pt window. Fix: make the last candidate the stacked one: ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) { HStack(spacing: 16) { icon; Text(metric.label); Spacer(); Text(metric.value) }; VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) { HStack { icon; Text(metric.label) }; Text(metric.value).foregroundStyle(.secondary) } }, with icon = Image(systemName: "chart.bar.fill").frame(width: iconSize) and @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body) private var iconSize: CGFloat = 32.

title: Workout name pinned to a fixed 120pt column
evidence: WorkoutRow fixes Text(workout.name).frame(width: 120) (line 14) in an HStack beside a fixed 24 x 24 icon frame (line 12) and .padding(). Measurement: 24pt icon + 120pt name + 3 HStack gaps (~8pt each) + 32pt padding = ~200pt committed before the value. A 17pt name fits ~13 characters per line in 120pt; at AX5 (53pt) it fits ~4 (estimate at ~0.55em per glyph), so a word like "Swimming" breaks mid-word and every name becomes a tall narrow column while the Spacer beside it stays empty. Configuration: AX5, any width. Fix: @Environment(\.dynamicTypeSize) private var typeSize; let layout = typeSize.isAccessibilitySize ? AnyLayout(VStackLayout(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4)) : AnyLayout(HStackLayout(alignment: .firstTextBaseline, spacing: 12)); layout { Image(systemName: "flame.fill").accessibilityHidden(true); Text(workout.name); Spacer(minLength: 8); Text(workout.calories, format: .number).monospacedDigit().foregroundStyle(.secondary).layoutPriority(1) }.

title: Row .padding() doubles the List's own insets
evidence: WorkoutRow adds .padding() (16pt on every side, line 19) and is used directly as a List row (line 27). List already applies its own row insets, so the content sits 16pt further in on both sides than system rows and each row grows up to 32pt taller. Fix: drop .padding() (at most .padding(.vertical, 4)) and adjust margins with .listRowInsets(_:) or .contentMargins(_:_:for:) when the design needs them.

title: Hamburger drawer is the iPhone's top-level navigation
evidence: TravelRoot hides its four top-level areas (Today, Trips, Saved, Settings) behind a line.3.horizontal toolbar button that slides a custom SideMenu over the NavigationStack (lines 34-50). Nothing on screen says what else exists, every area switch costs two taps instead of one, and the drawer is a website pattern. Its accessibility work (isModal, escape action, Reduce Motion transition) is careful but does not fix the model: four co-equal areas are a tab bar. Fix: TabView(selection: $area) { ForEach(Area.allCases) { a in Tab(a.title, systemImage: a.systemImage, value: a) { NavigationStack { AreaView(area: a).navigationTitle(a.title) } } } }.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable), and delete SideMenu, isMenuOpen and the Menu toolbar item.

title: Search field disappears when a search finds nothing
evidence: In the .loaded branch, .searchable is attached to the List (line 76), and that List is replaced by ContentUnavailableView.search when filter() returns nothing (lines 72-73). The moment a query matches no workout, the view carrying .searchable leaves the hierarchy, taking the search field and its Cancel button with it, while searchText keeps the query. Inferred from source: the user is left on No Results with no field to edit or clear, and the list does not come back until the screen is rebuilt (relaunch). A dead end on the screen's primary path, in an otherwise exemplary state model. State: zero results. Fix: keep the List and the modifier in the hierarchy and overlay the empty result: List(visible, selection: $selection) { WorkoutRow(workout: $0) }.overlay { if visible.isEmpty { ContentUnavailableView.search(text: searchText) } }.searchable(text: $searchText).

title: Workout name field tagged as a person's name
evidence: The Edit Workout name field sets .textContentType(.name) (line 189). That content type tells AutoFill the field wants a person's name, so the QuickType bar offers the user's own name from their contact card as a workout title. Fix: no content type on a free-text title: TextField("Name", text: $draft.name).textInputAutocapitalization(.words).focused($isNameFocused).submitLabel(.done).

title: Number and decimal pads have no way to dismiss
evidence: Card number uses .keyboardType(.numberPad) (line 12) and Amount uses .decimalPad (line 14); neither keyboard has a return key, and the form has no keyboard-toolbar Done, no @FocusState and no .scrollDismissesKeyboard. Once a numeric field is focused the keyboard stays up over the lower part of the form, and Pay is reachable only if it happens to sit above it. Fix: @FocusState private var focus: Field?; .focused($focus, equals: .card) and .focused($focus, equals: .amount) on the fields, and on the Form: .scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively).toolbar { ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .keyboard) { Spacer(); Button("Done") { focus = nil } } }.

title: Payment fields carry no textContentType
evidence: Neither "Name on card" (line 10) nor "Card number" (line 11) sets a textContentType, so AutoFill cannot offer a saved card or the cardholder's name, and every payment is typed by hand: 16 digits on a number pad that cannot be dismissed. Fix: TextField("Name on card", text: $name).textContentType(.name) and TextField("Card number", text: $cardNumber).keyboardType(.numberPad).textContentType(.creditCardNumber).

title: Pay has no validation, in-flight, error or success path
evidence: Button("Pay") { submit() } (line 16) calls an empty submit() (line 21): no field validation, no focus move to the first invalid field, no in-flight state or double-tap guard, no error state and no confirmation. A malformed card number gets no message, a double tap on any implementation of this shape charges twice, and a successful payment looks identical to a failed one. Flow step: Payment, submit (the only step). Fix: Button { guard !isPaying else { return }; if let bad = firstInvalidField() { focus = bad; return }; isPaying = true; Task { defer { isPaying = false }; do { try await pay(); didPay = true } catch { payError = error } } } label: { if isPaying { ProgressView() } else { Text("Pay") } }.disabled(isPaying), plus inline errors under the failing fields, an alert bound to payError that keeps every field intact, and a confirmation state on success.

title: Like and Comments use a web icon set
evidence: The bottom bar mixes ShareLink's SF Symbol (line 31) with Remix Icon assets ri-heart-fill / ri-heart-line (line 34) and ri-chat-3-line (line 42), resized into fixed 22pt frames. The bundled glyphs do not match the symbol's weight, optical size or baseline, ignore Bold Text, and cannot take a symbol effect, so the like state flips with a hard cut. SF Symbols cover both concepts. Fix: Button { isLiked.toggle() } label: { Label("Like", systemImage: isLiked ? "heart.fill" : "heart").contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace)) } and Button { isShowingComments = true } label: { Label("Comments", systemImage: "bubble.left") }; drop the 22pt frames and the glyph ScaledMetric, since symbols scale with the bar's text style.

title: Delete All erases everything without confirmation or undo
evidence: The toolbar's Delete All button (lines 19-22) runs workouts.removeAll() and store.deleteAll() on a single tap: no confirmation dialog, no count, no undo, and it stays enabled on an empty list. One mis-tap on the trailing toolbar slot destroys every record irreversibly. Fix: Button("Delete All", role: .destructive) { isConfirmingDeleteAll = true }.disabled(workouts.isEmpty) with .confirmationDialog("Delete \(workouts.count) workouts?", isPresented: $isConfirmingDeleteAll, titleVisibility: .visible) { Button("Delete All", role: .destructive) { workouts.removeAll(); Task { await store.deleteAll() } }; Button("Cancel", role: .cancel) { } } message: { Text("This can't be undone.") }.

title: Swipe-to-delete deletes permanently with no undo
evidence: The row .onDelete (lines 12-15) removes the row and calls store.deletePermanently(offsets) immediately. A full swipe commits without a second tap and nothing offers undo, so an accidental swipe destroys a workout for good. The store also receives index offsets rather than record IDs, so any change to the local order between the two calls deletes the wrong record. Fix: delete by identity and keep it reversible: .onDelete { offsets in pendingDelete = offsets.map { workouts[$0] }; workouts.remove(atOffsets: offsets) } with a visible Undo for at least 8 seconds that restores pendingDelete, committing store.deletePermanently(ids: pendingDelete.map(\.id)) only after it expires.

title: Overlay bottom bar permanently hides the last rows
evidence: The Record/Filter bar is attached with .overlay(alignment: .bottom) (line 12). An overlay does not change the List's safe area, so the list's bottom inset ignores the bar and the final rows scroll under it with no way to bring them above it. Measurement: one line of Label (~22pt at Large) plus .padding() 16pt top and bottom = ~54pt, more than a 44pt row, so the last row stays fully covered at the end of the scroll; at AX5 the bar grows and covers more. It looks correct in every screenshot that does not scroll to the end. Fix: replace the overlay with .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) { ... }, or better the system bar: .toolbar { ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .bottomBar) { Button("Record", systemImage: "plus.circle.fill") { }; Spacer(); Button("Filter", systemImage: "line.3.horizontal.decrease") { } } }.

title: Custom material bottom bar instead of the glass toolbar
evidence: The custom bar draws its own .background(.regularMaterial) slab (line 19) instead of using a bottomBar toolbar. On iOS 26+ the system toolbar renders its items as Liquid Glass, takes part in the glass accessibility adaptation and the user's Clear-to-Tinted setting, and applies the scroll edge effect; the material slab is the pre-26 look and sits as a flat band across the list. Fix: .toolbar { ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .bottomBar) { Button("Record", systemImage: "plus.circle.fill") { }; Spacer(); Button("Filter", systemImage: "line.3.horizontal.decrease") { } } }, the same change that fixes the overlay finding on line 12.

title: ignoresSafeArea on the ZStack puts controls under system UI
evidence: .ignoresSafeArea() is applied to the entire ZStack (line 66), so the control VStack and its .padding() are laid out against the physical screen edges, not only the camera preview. Measurement: the Close button's top sits 16pt from the top edge, inside the status bar and Dynamic Island band (top safe inset ~59pt on Dynamic Island iPhones), and the shutter button's bottom sits 16pt from the bottom edge, inside the 34pt home-indicator area where the system swipe-up competes with the tap. Fix: move the modifier to the background layer only: CameraPreview(session: camera.session).ignoresSafeArea().accessibilityLabel("Viewfinder"), and delete line 66.

title: Custom back button kills the interactive pop gesture
evidence: .navigationBarBackButtonHidden(true) (line 16) plus a hand-rolled topBarLeading Button calling dismiss() (lines 18-24). Hiding the system back button disables the edge-swipe back gesture, the most-used navigation gesture on iOS; the replacement reads "Back" instead of the parent's title, drops the long-press back history menu, and uses chevron.left, which does not mirror in right-to-left languages. Flow step: any pushed WorkoutDetail, returning to the list. Fix: delete .navigationBarBackButtonHidden(true) and the ToolbarItem; the system back button and the gesture come back.

title: Loading, empty and zero-results all render blank
evidence: WorkoutList renders List(visible) for every state (line 15): while .task awaits store.load() (line 20), when the user has no workouts, and when a search matches nothing, the screen is the same blank list under a title; load() cannot report failure, so there is no error state either. A new user cannot tell an empty account from a failed load, and a searcher gets no No Results message or way to relax the query. State: loading, empty, zero results, error (all absent in source). Fix: track isLoading and branch in an overlay: List(visible) { Text($0.name) }.overlay { if isLoading { ProgressView() } else if workouts.isEmpty { ContentUnavailableView { Label("No Workouts", systemImage: "figure.run") } description: { Text("Workouts you record appear here.") } actions: { Button("Record a Workout") { } } } else if visible.isEmpty { ContentUnavailableView.search(text: searchText) } }.

title: Case-sensitive search misses matching workouts
evidence: The filter uses $0.name.contains(searchText) (line 11), which is case- and diacritic-sensitive: "run" does not match "Morning Run" and "cafe" does not match "Café". People type lowercase, so searches return a false zero-results screen for workouts that exist. Fix: workouts.filter { $0.name.localizedStandardContains(searchText) }.

title: PillSwitch is a toggle look-alike with no accessibility
evidence: PillSwitch (lines 24-40) draws a switch from a Capsule and a Circle and flips the binding in .onTapGesture (line 38). It has no label, no button or toggle trait, no value, no Voice Control name, no keyboard access and no state animation, and the "Push notifications" Text beside it (lines 11-13) is a separate element. VoiceOver and Switch Control users cannot find or operate push notifications at all, while the Weekly digest row below uses a real Toggle. Fix: replace the HStack (lines 10-15) with Toggle("Push notifications", isOn: $pushEnabled).sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: pushEnabled); if the pill look is required, build it as a ToggleStyle whose makeBody draws the capsule and adds .accessibilityRepresentation { Toggle(isOn: configuration.$isOn) { configuration.label } }.

title: Near-black label literal is invisible in Dark Mode
evidence: "Push notifications" is colored Color(red: 0.11, green: 0.11, blue: 0.12) (line 12), a literal with no dark variant. Measurement (WCAG relative luminance, against Apple's published secondarySystemGroupedBackground values, not resolved at runtime): 1.00:1 on the Dark Mode grouped row (#1C1C1E) and 1.10:1 with Increase Contrast (#242426), against a 4.5:1 minimum; 17.00:1 on white in Light Mode. The label disappears for every Dark Mode user. WCAG: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), AA. Fix: delete the modifier (row text defaults to .primary) or use .foregroundStyle(.primary).

title: Compose draft lives in @State and dies on swipe-down
evidence: ComposeSheet owns subject and body_ as @State inside the presented sheet (lines 11-12) with no interactiveDismissDisabled, no Cancel button and no persistence. A reflexive swipe-down mid-message discards everything without a prompt, and backgrounding followed by termination loses it too; Send is enabled on an empty message. Flow step: Compose, the only step. Fix: own an @Observable ComposeDraft in InboxView and pass it in: .sheet(isPresented: $isComposing) { ComposeSheet(draft: draft).interactiveDismissDisabled(draft.hasContent) }; in the sheet add ToolbarItem(placement: .cancellationAction) { Button("Cancel") { draft.hasContent ? (isConfirmingDiscard = true) : dismiss() } } with a Discard Draft confirmationDialog, persist the draft when scenePhase leaves .active, and .disabled(draft.isEmpty) on Send.

title: Send dismisses before sending; failure is silent
evidence: send() fires Task { await api.send(...) } and calls dismiss() on the next line (lines 30-33), so the sheet closes before the request finishes. If the send fails (offline, rejected) the user is never told and the subject and body are already gone with the sheet; there is no in-flight state, no double-tap guard and no sent confirmation. Fix: make api.send throw and await it: Button { guard !isSending else { return }; isSending = true; Task { defer { isSending = false }; do { try await api.send(subject: draft.subject, body: draft.body); draft.clear(); dismiss() } catch { sendError = error } } } label: { if isSending { ProgressView() } else { Text("Send") } }.disabled(isSending || draft.isEmpty), with the failure in an alert bound to sendError and the draft kept (or queued in an Outbox the Inbox shows).
